question: On fast seed 119, does a coverage-fix (dense isophote fill → decimate → cross) close anchor starvation, and is single-shoot ω-aliasing the binding blocker?
hypothesis: Closing anchor starvation by coverage will let the s099 pipeline invert seed 119.
narrative_md: Coverage works: a 12M adaptive isophote fill drops anchor B's nearest-truth rep from a starved 10.5° to 0.68° (A to 1.02°). But the end-to-end inversion still lands top blind ρ 48.17, Band D, 0/15 Band A. Cause: the single finite-diff-init shoot on the truth-near pair connects to an ω 104° off truth at |ω| below the bracket → rejected; a bounded multi-start recovers it to 4.58°. Coverage is not the binding blocker — single-shoot ω-selection is. Blind pipeline; truth used only for labels/probe.
